reason: The hypothesis relies on a causal chain linking configurational entropy to homogeneous structure, electron-phonon coupling, and superconductivity. The cited evidence (E1, E2) only demonstrates that a specific HEA is superconducting at ambient pressure and that entropy correlates with pressure-robustness of Tc in a different material system; neither passage provides direct support for the key premises about entropy stabilizing a homogeneous matrix to promote Cooper pairing or that lowering entropy degrades Tc and volume fraction in the proposed manner.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes a homogeneous simple crystalline matrix in HEAs
This homogeneous matrix promotes robust electron-phonon mediated Cooper pairing despite atomic disorder
Lowering configurational entropy by partial substitution degrades this stabilizing effect
Degrading the stabilizing effect lowers Tc and reduces superconducting volume fraction
The cited evidence shows entropy enhances robustness of superconductivity against external pressure
